holidays.name: National Escargot Day
holidays.description: A day for snail lovers and the adventurous eaters who are curious about them. Traditionally the dish is snails bathed in garlic-parsley butter and served sizzling, so it's a day to put on your fanciest fork and say bonjour to your inner Parisian.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance of unclear origin, celebrating the classic French delicacy of cooked land snails.
holidays.funFact: The word escargot is simply French for snail, and the dish is often served in special dimpled pans or tongs-and-fork sets made just for holding the shells.

holidays.name: Tiara Day
holidays.description: A sparkly excuse to crown yourself in rhinestones. Whether you're going to brunch, a meeting, or just feeding the cat, today is the day to wear a tiara and carry yourself like royalty.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin, celebrating glitz, glamour, and the joy of dressing up for no reason at all.
holidays.funFact: The word tiara comes from a Greek and Latin term for a headdress. Tiaras were once worn mostly by Persian kings, and later by the Pope.

holidays.name: National Scavenger Hunt Day
holidays.description: A day for hiding, seeking, and bragging rights. Gather friends or family, write up a list of clues and silly items, and race around the neighborhood to find everything first.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin, celebrating the classic party game of searching for hidden objects or clues.
holidays.funFact: Scavenger hunts are often credited to the socialite Elsa Maxwell, who popularized them at 1930s high-society parties, famously sending guests off to fetch odd items.
